resources.string: Use from the hotbar to restore %1$d health. Not consumed when health is full.
Equip in the hotbar. Pickaxes mine rock and ores; axes cut wood; shovels dig soil. Wood → stone → iron → steel improves speed. Tools also defend against nearby creatures and do not wear out.

Pulls one item a second from the container above (a machine gives only its products) into its own small stock, and pours it into the container it points at. Set it against the block it should pour into, or on a floor to pour down. Hoppers in a row carry items along.
Keep in your backpack to grind wheat into flour or corn into cornmeal through crafting. A powered grain mill gives three times as much.
Your stock of one item is full. Empty this chest before breaking it.
Drag a stack between bag, bar and storage. Tap for details; hold to split, adjust the amount, then tap outside. Breaking this block returns its contents.
Add wheat for flour or corn for cornmeal. It turns on a vertical shaft coming down onto it, or against a side of a gearbox. 1 crop → 3 ground ingredients; faster when it turns faster.
Power connected. Add wheat: 1 wheat → 3 flour in 6 seconds. Close this panel to resume production.

Select the dish in the production menu, then add ingredients and coal or charcoal. Each batch takes 1 fuel: meats, soups, gratins, pies, fish and desserts. Recipes using milk return the empty bucket. Close the panel to cook.
3 identical harvested crops → 1 compost in 20 seconds. Use compost on a growing crop to speed it up. Close the panel to resume.

Gather wood and stone, craft tools, then explore for wayfarer caches and new seeds. Tools speed up matching materials. Irrigation and light improve crops; harvests can become seeds, meals or compost. Equip food in the hotbar and use it to heal. Use a chest or machine to open its storage; crouch to place against it. A hopper moves one item per second from the container above into the one below. Machines turn with a wheel or a crank, through shafts and gears. These systems do not change Assault mode.
Join sails together in front of the head, then use it: the sails turn and drive the axle behind it. Use it again to stop them and put them back. Each sail adds force; the wind is always the same.
At least %1$d sails joined in front of the head.
Some sails had no room and went back to your bag.
Place it so that flowing or falling water runs through its paddles: the current sets which way it turns. It turns the axle through its hub. The large wheel turns half as fast and is twice as strong.
Turns with the axle it continues. Two cogwheels side by side turn opposite ways; a large and a small one set diagonally double or halve the speed. A gearbox turns the rotation a quarter turn.
Place it on a side of a gearbox. Use it again and again to keep it turning. Little force.
Stopped · not enough force: add a wheel or remove a machine.
Stopped · parts turn against each other.
Place and use a hearth to bind it. The talisman takes you home and back to where you left. Recharge: 20 seconds of play. A clear landing is required.
Hearth bound. Use your talisman to return here.
No destination bound, or the hearth was removed.
No safe, clear landing near the destination.
Resonance has guided you to your destination.
Local trade · 8 batches per offer, renewed every 10 minutes of play. A gathering bell also welcomes traders at your home.
Trade unavailable: depleted stock, missing items or trader too far away.
Animal fed. Two nearby adults ready to breed can have a baby.
Product collected. Feed this animal for its next production.
This animal is growing, digesting or still preparing its product.

Lure and feed cows and sheep with wheat, pigs with carrots, chickens with wheat seeds. Two fed adults of the same species in the same pen approach and breed, then rest for 5 minutes. Leave space: at most 24 animals within 12 blocks. Young animals mature in 10 minutes nearby; each meal saves 2 minutes. Milk: empty bucket; wool: shears; eggs and truffles: empty hand. Products are ready 2 minutes after feeding. Use an empty hand on an animal to check its state. Killed adults give meat to cook; young animals give none.

Needs rotation from a gearbox: place it against one of its sides, never straight on a shaft. A row of gearboxes shares its force between the workshops beside it. Deposit ingredients; recipes run automatically.
The kiln uses raw coal for each batch.
The vat turns milk into cheese, butter or cream. Select the product in the production menu before adding milk. Empty buckets are returned.
Unable to save. The previous checkpoint is preserved.

Hamlets welcome a gardener, artisan and keeper. Use a nearby resident to trade. A crafted gathering bell welcomes this trio at your home. Workshops connect two chains: ore → dust → metal → plates and gears; wool → cloth and milk → cheese. Crushers, presses and looms require a waterwheel; kilns, vats and kitchens need no transmission. Hoppers extract finished products.
Place and use a resonance hearth, then craft a talisman to return home and resume your expedition.
Animals can be fed, bred and harvested without slaughter. Walls now block the light used for spawning. Light your indoor rooms.

Deposit wheat, carrots and wheat seeds. Feeds animals within 4 blocks for growth, production and breeding. At most one meal every 30 seconds, only when useful. Hoppers can supply the trough. Leave space for young animals.
Choose a recipe to reserve its ingredients: a hopper underneath then extracts only that recipe’s products. Automatic mode prioritizes the first available recipe.

Add charcoal or coal. Embers melt copper and fire glass and clay; bellows beside the forge, turning from a gearbox, bring red heat (iron) at speed 16 and white heat (steel) at 32. The hotter, the faster the fuel burns.
Meat collected. Cook it in a cooking stove.
Young animal: about %1$d min of growth remaining nearby. A meal saves 2 min; meals are 30 s apart.
Feed this animal %1$s to start production. Feed two adults of the same species in the same pen to breed them.
Product ready in about %1$d min nearby. Extra meals do not speed up production.
Milk ready: use an empty bucket on this cow.
Wool ready: use shears on this sheep.
Product ready: select an empty hotbar slot, then use this animal.
Meat comes from adult cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. Young animals give no meat. Cook raw meat in a cooking stove; it cannot be eaten raw.
Cooking ingredient. Use the recipes button to see how to make and use it. Select butter or cream in the vat before adding milk; empty buckets are returned.
Select the dish in the station production menu before adding ingredients and fuel. Close the inventory to let time pass. Hand preparations are in the crafting menu.
